scope_gate.source: Parent-provided frozen eligibility gate; auditor did not modify status or PR.
scope_gate.claimed_subquestion: 1998 item5(b), one of five catalogue subquestions

exact_claim: There exists a smooth one-parameter family of flat torsion-free affine connections D^t=D^0+t dx tensor dx tensor partial_y on the fixed compact torus, starting from the standard positive Hessian structure at t=0, such that no positive definite Hessian metric exists for any t!=0. Consequently unrestricted small affine-structure deformations need not preserve Hessian metric existence.
assumptions: Positive definite Hessian means a Riemannian metric with local Hessian potentials relative to the flat torsion-free connection.
Existence of any Hessian metric, not preservation of a specified metric, is the property being tested.
Affine holonomy is allowed to vary; no hyperbolic-developing-domain hypothesis is imposed.
decision_reason: The exact affine-torus family is present in Baues-Goldman2004v1 pp24-25. Delanoe1989 Theoreme3 p67 prescribes its hypothetical Hessian volume; Jorgens1954 Satz1 p130 forces the resulting entire developing potential to be quadratic; positive definite constant metrics cannot be invariant under its nonzero unipotent shear holonomy. This proves nonexistence of all Hessian metrics using old primary results, not just of parallel candidates.

additional_routes.corroborates: parallel-volume replacement result attributed to Cheng-Yau1982
